summary: Polk County tower moved here from Providence in 1990; the newest account found (2006) says it stood, and no later status was found.

facts.design: 100-foot tower topped by a cubicle-sized room, 132 steps
facts.status_note: Last described as standing in a 2006 newspaper account; no later source found.

access.note: In 2006 the owner was the Florida Division of Forestry, and the structures were described as no longer considered safe.

events.note: Eastern US Lookouts says a lookout tower was erected at Providence in 1963; a 2006 newspaper dates the Green Swamp Tower's construction to 1963 and does not mention a move.
The Providence tower was dismantled into three sections, moved about two miles north and re-erected as the Green Swamp tower.
Officially retired; structures described as no longer considered safe; antenna still attached, radio gone.

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict on the 1963 build: the Providence page says a tower was erected there in 1963 and moved to Green Swamp in 1990, while the 2006 article says the Green Swamp Tower was constructed in 1963 and mentions no move. Not resolved. The newest source is from 2006 and no later status was found, so the record's gone status is unsupported and should be checked against Florida Forest Service records. The Ledger's own pages (2006 and 2015) returned 403 to fetch_text; a 2015 Ledger article on Polk's towers was seen only as a search snippet and is not cited.
